pr_title: sql: prevent dropping enum values used in index partitioning or predicates
pr_body:
This commit adds logic to detect usages of enum values in partitioning clauses
and in index predicates.

Fixes #63366.

Release note (bug fix): Fixed a bug which permitted the dropping of enum values
which were in use in index predicates or partitioning values.
pr_comments: This change is [](https://reviewable.io/reviews/cockroachdb/cockroach/68257)

These test failures are surprising. This one particularly:
```
statement ok
CREATE DATABASE repartition_privs PRIMARY REGION "ca-central-1" REGIONS "us-east-1";
CREATE TABLE repartition_privs.rbr () LOCALITY REGIONAL BY ROW;

....

statement ok
ALTER DATABASE repartition_privs DROP REGION "us-east-1"
```

I can't help but wonder if it's even legal to drop a region when there's a REGIONAL BY ROW table. It seems to me that this should only be possible once we've validated that the table has no rows for which the region column's value is the one to be dropped.

> This kind of code makes me wish we could routinely transform the descriptor state back into a fully decorated AST (the kind that would trivially map to some SHOW CREATE output) because then implementing these kinds of checks becomes easy-peasy.

I'm not seeing how it would be easy peasy. We do have logic to convert the descriptors back to SHOW CREATE but it relies on a very large pile of machinery. 

> I can't help but wonder if it's even legal to drop a region when there's a REGIONAL BY ROW table. It seems to me that this should only be possible once we've validated that the table has no rows for which the region column's value is the one to be dropped.

Err, yeah, I need to look into that 😓
I'm saying _writing the checks in this PR_ would be easy-peasy: for each type back-reference, visit each node of the corresponding AST, check that none match the enum value to drop.

> I can't help but wonder if it's even legal to drop a region when there's a REGIONAL BY ROW table.

We have something that checks that no row has that value before we drop it. @arulajmani can tell you more away from code search atm :)

> We have something that checks that no row has that value before we drop it. @arulajmani can tell you more away from code search atm :)

It's this very code I'm changing now. I've reworked things to repartition in the same transaction that does the check. I'll see what happens with the tests but this now mostly works.

issue_context.title: sql: PARTITIONING on an ENUM and using DROP VALUE on it returns an error
issue_context.body:
Consider:

```
SET enable_drop_enum_value = true;
create type t as enum('a', 'b', 'c');
create table tbl (pk t PRIMARY KEY) PARTITION BY LIST (pk) (PARTITION "a" VALUES IN ('a'));
alter partition "a" of table tbl configure zone using gc.ttlseconds = 1;
alter type t drop value 'a';
```

Now the tbl is broken:
